The Linen Story

Designed by nature for warmer living.

Linen is spun from flax — a long, hollow fibre that moves air and moisture rather than holding them. It is why the fabric has always belonged to hot places.

Read the linen story
  1. 01

    Breathability

    Linen's hollow fibre and open weave let warm air pass instead of trapping it.

  2. 02

    Lightweight comfort

    Less cloth against the skin, so a full day in the sun stays wearable.

  3. 03

    Natural texture

    Slubs and small irregularities are part of the yarn, not a flaw in it.

  4. 04

    Moisture management

    Linen absorbs moisture readily and releases it quickly into the air.

  5. 05

    Timeless appeal

    A fabric that has dressed warm climates for centuries, and still reads modern.

Craft

Considered in every detail.

Small decisions — collar structure, cuff width, stitch density — are what separate a linen shirt that lasts a season from one that lasts years.

The collar

Lightly fused so it holds its line without stiffness.

The cuff

Two-button adjustment, sized to sit clean under a watch.

The weave

Open enough to breathe, dense enough to keep its shape.
